Hi Jordan and team — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise PII handling summary you can share with procurement/legal. Happy to jump on a call if you want to walk through any item.

PII handling summary — Redwood Inference (for hosted API unless otherwise noted):

- Storage of prompts/outputs: By default, we persist request/response payloads in encrypted logs to support observability, billing, and troubleshooting. These logs can include prompt inputs and model outputs if the customer does not opt out.
- Default retention: For standard hosted accounts, request/response logs are retained for 30 days by default. Retention can be configured per-customer (shorter retention periods available) as part of an enterprise agreement.
- Training usage: Redwood does not use customer prompts/outputs for model training or to improve models unless there is an explicit opt-in in the customer contract. For Dedicated and Private deployments, training access is never enabled.
- Ability to disable storage/logging: Customers can disable request/response logging for specific routes or for the entire account on Dedicated or Private deployments. For hosted accounts, we offer a logging-disable option under enterprise contracts; there is an additional configuration and SLA tradeoff (loss of some observability).
- Data residency: We provide region-scoped hosting (US, EU). For EU residency requirements, we can ensure that processing and storage remain in EU regions for hosted traffic routed to our EU endpoints. If you require strict contractual data residency and control, our Dedicated or Private options provide stronger guarantees (customer-managed VPC/on-prem).
- Audit evidence & access logs: We can provide SOC2 artifacts, access logs, and deletion confirmations as part of the enterprise compliance package. Standard hosted accounts receive basic access logs; enterprise customers can request extended retention of audit logs and SOC2 evidence under an add-on.
- Deletion & DSARs: We support account-level data deletion requests and will provide confirmation of deletion. For DSAR/ER requests, please follow our data subject request process; we will coordinate with Acme's privacy team.

Next steps we propose:
- I can provide a one-page statement for procurement summarizing the bullets above and include the redwood-pii-dataflow-diagram.png and SOC2-summary.pdf (attached).
- If Acme requires EU-only residency for hosted traffic, we will configure your account to use our EU endpoints. For contractual residency guarantees or to avoid any cross-border routing, recommend Dedicated or Private deployment — we can provide pricing/lead time for those options.
- If helpful, schedule a 30-minute meeting this week between Acme procurement/legal and our security/solutions leads — here is a suggested slot: https://calendar.redwood.ai/meeting/rdw-acme-pii-review

Let me know if you need any of the bullets in different legal wording.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
